match.reason: None of the bank points teaches the role of consumers in deciding what businesses make; the closest matches cover consumer behaviour assumptions, ethics, legal definitions, economy-wide interdependence, or surplus, which are different ideas or depths.

draft.title: The role of consumers
card: A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods and services. Goods are things you can touch, such as shoes. Services are things done for you, such as a haircut.
something a person must have to live and be well, such as food, water, shelter and clothing.
something a person would like to have but can live without, such as a new game console or concert tickets.
Consumers spend money to meet their needs and wants. Businesses watch what people buy and make more of what sells well. In this way, consumers' spending helps decide what businesses make.
draft.remember: Consumers buy to meet needs and wants, and their spending guides what businesses make.

a.q: Which of these is a consumer buying a service?
opts: Paying a mechanic to repair a car
Buying a new pair of running shoes
Buying a loaf of bread at a bakery
Buying a phone from an electronics shop
a.why: A repair is work done for the buyer, so it is a service. Running shoes, bread and a phone are things you can touch, so they are goods. Shoes are tempting because they are bought by a consumer, but they are a good.
a.clue: Which one is work done for you, not a thing you hold?

b.q: Many shoppers in Wagga Wagga start buying oat milk instead of dairy milk. Over time, the local supermarket stocks more oat milk. What does this show about consumers?
opts: Their spending helps decide what businesses supply
Their spending is decided by what the supermarket stocks
Their needs change whenever a new product appears
Their wants must be met before their needs
b.why: Shoppers changed what they bought, and the supermarket then changed what it stocked. This shows consumer spending helping to decide what businesses make or supply. The reverse option is tempting, but here the shoppers acted first and the shop followed.
b.clue: Who changed their behaviour first, the shoppers or the shop?

a.best: Paying a mechanic to repair a car

b.best: Their spending helps decide what businesses supply
